validated_work_order.root_cause: Account.tsx `canCalculateBalance()` returns true only when the sort is absent, or is `field === 'date' && ascDesc === 'desc'`. It is a direction gate, not a data gate, and the direction it gates on is not a property of the data - it is a property of how the balance query happens to be built. When it returns false, (a) `calculateBalances()` short-circuits and returns `null`, so `state.balances` is nulled by the `onData` handler; (b) `render()` passes `showBalances={!!allBalances}`, and `allBalances` is that same null, so `showBalances` is false; (c) `visibleColumns` in TransactionsTable filters the 'balance' column out of the render list, removing the header cell and every row cell; and (d) `onManageColumns()` filters it out of the list passed to the modal, which is why the toggle vanishes. So the loss of the column and the loss of the toggle are one condition. The gate exists because `calculateBalances()` builds its `$sumOver` window from `this.paged.query`, which already carries the user's display sort; `$sumOver` compiles (compiler.ts:550-560) to `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY <the query's own orderExpressions> ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)`, and that frame only yields a running balance when the ordering runs newest-to-oldest. Under date/asc the same frame sums each row forward toward newer transactions and returns wrong numbers - measured at the SQL layer as 75 / -25 / 25 where 100 / 50 / 75 is correct - so the guard suppresses the column rather than showing them. The bug is that the correct answer was made unreachable instead of computed: the running balance of a transaction is a property of that transaction, not of the display order, and the display sort is only being used as the window's frame.

  FIXED (new Query({...state, orderExpressions:[{date:'desc'}]}))

  FIXED + tiebreaker ([{date:'desc'},{sort_order:'desc'}])
                                                       -> [{t3,75},{t2,50},{t1,100}]             correct
  NEGATIVE: .orderBy({date:'asc'}).orderBy({date:'desc'}) -> orderExpressions serialize to
            [{date:'asc'},{date:'desc'}] and the result is [{t1,75},{t2,-25},{t3,25}]   STILL WRONG
  FILTERS SURVIVE the rebuild (account + reconciled filters carried through) -> [{t3,75},{t2,50},{t1,100}]

  Command: `cd packages/loot-core && ENV=node npx vitest --run src/server/aql/sdlc-probe.test.ts` (scratch file deleted afterwards).

  Two rows here are load-bearing and neither is visible from reading the code. (1) The NEGATIVE row: `Query.orderBy` APPENDS to orderExpressions rather than replacing them, so the tempting one-liner of appending `{date:'desc'}` leaves the user's ascending sort in front and silently changes nothing - the bug would appear unfixed. The array must be replaced wholesale. (2) The FIXED rows use `new Query({ ...query.serialize(), orderExpressions })`; note that `serialize()` emits the key `selectExpressions`, not `select`. An earlier form of this probe that spread the serialized state and then set a `select` key returned rows with NO balance field at all, because the real `selectExpressions` was overwritten by a key the deserializer ignores - a silent, empty-looking result rather than an error. Replace `orderExpressions` on the serialized state and change nothing else.

validated_work_order.approach:
Make the running balance independent of the display sort direction, then drop the direction clause from `canCalculateBalance()` so the column and its toggle survive an ascending sort.

In `Account.tsx`, build the balance query so its window ordering is always newest-to-oldest, independent of `this.paged.query`'s user sort. Concretely: take the paged query's serialized state, replace `orderExpressions` wholesale with `[{ date: 'desc' }, { sort_order: 'desc' }]` (the second entry mirrors the tiebreaker `applySort` appends, so equal-date rows stay deterministic), and keep everything else - filters, `options({ splits: 'none' })`, table - untouched.

Two traps, both measured rather than reasoned (see evidence): `Query.orderBy` APPENDS to `orderExpressions`, so appending `{date:'desc'}` leaves the user's ascending sort in front and the fix does nothing; and `serialize()` emits `selectExpressions`, so spread the serialized state and replace ONLY `orderExpressions` - setting a `select` key silently drops the selection and returns rows with no balance at all. `new Query({ ...state, orderExpressions })` is the form verified to work at the SQL layer. `Account.tsx` currently imports `Query` as a type only (line 20); constructing one needs the value import.

Then relax `canCalculateBalance()` from `sort.field === 'date' && sort.ascDesc === 'desc'` to accept a date sort in either direction. Keep returning false for a non-date sort field, a non-empty `search`, and non-empty `filterConditions` - those genuinely make a running balance meaningless, because a filtered set does not accumulate to the account total. Both were confirmed working today and must survive.

Once the guard no longer excludes ascending, all three consumers follow from the one change: `state.balances` stops being nulled, `showBalances={!!allBalances}` stays true so `visibleColumns` keeps the column, and `onManageColumns()` keeps passing the balance column to the modal so the toggle stays available. `grep` confirms exactly three callers of the guard, all in this file: the reconciled-rows filter (line 485), `calculateBalances()` (line 706), and `onManageColumns()` (line 932).

Put the query construction in a small exported pure helper in its own file under `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/` (e.g. `balanceQuery.ts`), so it can be unit-tested. This is not cosmetic: `vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`, so a test placed next to the helper is the only regression test CI actually runs for this change. The e2e cases stay in `tests[]` regardless - they are the right regression test for a human running the suite.

Prefer this over simply deleting the guard: deleting it alone would render the Balance column with the wrong numbers measured at the SQL layer (75 / -25 / 25), trading a missing column for a silently wrong one. The values must stay correct under ascending display, not merely present.

Do not change `$sumOver` in compiler.ts. The CURRENT ROW -> UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING frame is a correct, general window; the bug is that a display sort is allowed to define it. `calculateRunningBalancesTopDown` in `hooks/useTransactions.ts` is the mobile equivalent and already handles ascending; it is a separate client-side path and is out of scope.

The selection survives the rebuild: the returned query still serializes `selectExpressions` to `[{balance:{$sumOver:'$amount'}}]`. This pins the trap measured at the SQL layer, where spreading the serialized state and adding a `select` key silently produced rows with no balance field at all.

Rebuilding preserves every filter: the helper's output carries the same `filterExpressions` as its input, so the account filter and the reconciled-rows filter added at Account.tsx:483-488 survive and the balances are not computed over a wider row set than the table shows.

A query that already has no orderExpressions gains the explicit newest-first ordering rather than being left unordered, so the balance window is deterministic on first load before any sort is applied.
A query already ordered `{date:'desc'}` round-trips unchanged, pinning that the fix is a no-op for the currently-working direction and cannot regress it.

risks: The most likely wrong fix is deleting the ascDesc guard without making the window order-independent. That turns a missing column into a silently WRONG column: the AQL probe measured date-asc returning 75/-25/25 instead of 100/50/75. AC-2 exists specifically to catch that, and reviewers should treat a diff that only touches `canCalculateBalance()` as incomplete.

`Query.orderBy` appends to `orderExpressions` rather than replacing them, so naively appending `{ date: 'desc' }` to the existing query leaves the user's ascending sort in front and silently changes nothing - measured at the SQL layer, the appended query still returns 75/-25/25 and the bug would appear unfixed. The helper must replace the array wholesale.

`serialize()` emits `selectExpressions`, not `select`. Spreading the serialized state into `new Query({...state, select: [...]})` silently replaces the real selection with a key the deserializer ignores, and the query returns rows with NO balance field at all - an empty-looking result rather than an error, which is easy to mistake for 'the column is empty'. Replace `orderExpressions` on the serialized state and change nothing else.

The balance query is built from `this.paged.query`, which also carries any active filters and the reconciled-rows filter applied at Account.tsx:483-488. Replacing `orderExpressions` must not also drop `filterExpressions`, or the balances will be computed over a different row set than the table shows. A unit test asserts the filters survive.

`onSaveColumns` (Account.tsx:988-1005) has a side effect when the balance column is re-enabled: it clears `transactions`, `filterConditions`, `search`, and `sort`, then refetches. If the modal now offers the balance toggle in states where it previously did not, this reset will fire in more situations. Verify it does not silently discard a user's search or filter without the UI saying so.

The account page also uses `canCalculateBalance()` for the reconciled-rows filter (Account.tsx:483-488). Relaxing the guard changes which rows are loaded when reconciled transactions are hidden - correct in principle (it matches what date/desc already does), but it is a second behavioural effect of the same change and should be checked, not assumed. AC-5 exercises the round trip.

Making the balance column appear under conditions where it previously did not means more users will hit the balance query path; it is a `$sumOver` window over the account's transactions, so its cost on very large accounts should be sanity-checked.

This repository is an imported snapshot (a single 'Import actualbudget/actual' commit), so `git log -S` / `git blame` on `canCalculateBalance` yields no history and cannot say when the guard was introduced or why. The intent behind the direction check is inferred from the `$sumOver` frame semantics and the AQL probe, not from a commit message. An implementer with upstream history available should sanity-check that inference.

approved_work_order.root_cause: Account.tsx `canCalculateBalance()` returns true only when the sort is absent, or is `field === 'date' && ascDesc === 'desc'`. It is a direction gate, not a data gate, and the direction it gates on is not a property of the data - it is a property of how the balance query happens to be built. When it returns false, (a) `calculateBalances()` short-circuits and returns `null`, so `state.balances` is nulled by the `onData` handler; (b) `render()` passes `showBalances={!!allBalances}`, and `allBalances` is that same null, so `showBalances` is false; (c) `visibleColumns` in TransactionsTable filters the 'balance' column out of the render list, removing the header cell and every row cell; and (d) `onManageColumns()` filters it out of the list passed to the modal, which is why the toggle vanishes. So the loss of the column and the loss of the toggle are one condition. The gate exists because `calculateBalances()` builds its `$sumOver` window from `this.paged.query`, which already carries the user's display sort; `$sumOver` compiles (compiler.ts:550-560) to `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY <the query's own orderExpressions> ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)`, and that frame only yields a running balance when the ordering runs newest-to-oldest. Under date/asc the same frame sums each row forward toward newer transactions and returns wrong numbers - measured at the SQL layer as 75 / -25 / 25 where 100 / 50 / 75 is correct - so the guard suppresses the column rather than showing them. The bug is that the correct answer was made unreachable instead of computed: the running balance of a transaction is a property of that transaction, not of the display order, and the display sort is only being used as the window's frame.

approved_work_order.approach:
Make the running balance independent of the display sort direction, then drop the direction clause from `canCalculateBalance()` so the column and its toggle survive an ascending sort.

In `Account.tsx`, build the balance query so its window ordering is always newest-to-oldest, independent of `this.paged.query`'s user sort. Concretely: take the paged query's serialized state, replace `orderExpressions` wholesale with `[{ date: 'desc' }, { sort_order: 'desc' }]` (the second entry mirrors the tiebreaker `applySort` appends, so equal-date rows stay deterministic), and keep everything else - filters, `options({ splits: 'none' })`, table - untouched.

Two traps, both measured rather than reasoned (see evidence): `Query.orderBy` APPENDS to `orderExpressions`, so appending `{date:'desc'}` leaves the user's ascending sort in front and the fix does nothing; and `serialize()` emits `selectExpressions`, so spread the serialized state and replace ONLY `orderExpressions` - setting a `select` key silently drops the selection and returns rows with no balance at all. `new Query({ ...state, orderExpressions })` is the form verified to work at the SQL layer. `Account.tsx` currently imports `Query` as a type only (line 20); constructing one needs the value import.

Then relax `canCalculateBalance()` from `sort.field === 'date' && sort.ascDesc === 'desc'` to accept a date sort in either direction. Keep returning false for a non-date sort field, a non-empty `search`, and non-empty `filterConditions` - those genuinely make a running balance meaningless, because a filtered set does not accumulate to the account total. Both were confirmed working today and must survive.

Once the guard no longer excludes ascending, all three consumers follow from the one change: `state.balances` stops being nulled, `showBalances={!!allBalances}` stays true so `visibleColumns` keeps the column, and `onManageColumns()` keeps passing the balance column to the modal so the toggle stays available. `grep` confirms exactly three callers of the guard, all in this file: the reconciled-rows filter (line 485), `calculateBalances()` (line 706), and `onManageColumns()` (line 932).

Put the query construction in a small exported pure helper in its own file under `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/` (e.g. `balanceQuery.ts`), so it can be unit-tested. This is not cosmetic: `vite.config.mts` collects only `src/**`, so a test placed next to the helper is the only regression test CI actually runs for this change. The e2e cases stay in `tests[]` regardless - they are the right regression test for a human running the suite.

Prefer this over simply deleting the guard: deleting it alone would render the Balance column with the wrong numbers measured at the SQL layer (75 / -25 / 25), trading a missing column for a silently wrong one. The values must stay correct under ascending display, not merely present.

Do not change `$sumOver` in compiler.ts. The CURRENT ROW -> UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING frame is a correct, general window; the bug is that a display sort is allowed to define it. `calculateRunningBalancesTopDown` in `hooks/useTransactions.ts` is the mobile equivalent and already handles ascending; it is a separate client-side path and is out of scope.

risks: The most likely wrong fix is deleting the ascDesc guard without making the window order-independent. That turns a missing column into a silently WRONG column: the AQL probe measured date-asc returning 75/-25/25 instead of 100/50/75. AC-2 exists specifically to catch that, and reviewers should treat a diff that only touches `canCalculateBalance()` as incomplete.

`Query.orderBy` appends to `orderExpressions` rather than replacing them, so naively appending `{ date: 'desc' }` to the existing query leaves the user's ascending sort in front and silently changes nothing - measured at the SQL layer, the appended query still returns 75/-25/25 and the bug would appear unfixed. The helper must replace the array wholesale.

`serialize()` emits `selectExpressions`, not `select`. Spreading the serialized state into `new Query({...state, select: [...]})` silently replaces the real selection with a key the deserializer ignores, and the query returns rows with NO balance field at all - an empty-looking result rather than an error, which is easy to mistake for 'the column is empty'. Replace `orderExpressions` on the serialized state and change nothing else.

The balance query is built from `this.paged.query`, which also carries any active filters and the reconciled-rows filter applied at Account.tsx:483-488. Replacing `orderExpressions` must not also drop `filterExpressions`, or the balances will be computed over a different row set than the table shows. A unit test asserts the filters survive.

`onSaveColumns` (Account.tsx:988-1005) has a side effect when the balance column is re-enabled: it clears `transactions`, `filterConditions`, `search`, and `sort`, then refetches. If the modal now offers the balance toggle in states where it previously did not, this reset will fire in more situations. Verify it does not silently discard a user's search or filter without the UI saying so.

The account page also uses `canCalculateBalance()` for the reconciled-rows filter (Account.tsx:483-488). Relaxing the guard changes which rows are loaded when reconciled transactions are hidden - correct in principle (it matches what date/desc already does), but it is a second behavioural effect of the same change and should be checked, not assumed. AC-5 exercises the round trip.

Making the balance column appear under conditions where it previously did not means more users will hit the balance query path; it is a `$sumOver` window over the account's transactions, so its cost on very large accounts should be sanity-checked.

This repository is an imported snapshot (a single 'Import actualbudget/actual' commit), so `git log -S` / `git blame` on `canCalculateBalance` yields no history and cannot say when the guard was introduced or why. The intent behind the direction check is inferred from the `$sumOver` frame semantics and the AQL probe, not from a commit message. An implementer with upstream history available should sanity-check that inference.

alternatives_considered.approach: Just delete the sort-direction clause from `canCalculateBalance()` so the column always shows.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The column would render with wrong numbers. `$sumOver` compiles to `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY <query orders> ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)` and the frame direction is fixed, so under date/asc it sums forward toward newer rows. Measured at the SQL layer: 75/-25/25 where 100/50/75 is correct. Replaces a visible bug with a silent data bug.
